thread:
maria: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selector change we see p99 latency bump for cold prefixes in eu-west when traffic routes cross zones. Noticed bigger tail when queue drains trigger cross-cluster spill.
ajay: Copy. Do you have profiling traces? where is KV hit-rate going?
maria: Uploading a short flame and kv stats. KV hit drops ~12% on cross-zone requests. Flame shows more time in KVCopy + network wait when we spill to standby cluster.
kevin: That smells like our cache sharding + affinity logic. If affinity fails, request goes to remote cluster and we rebuild KV cache from scratch.
lina: Can you paste the batching config used in eu-west? maybe batch formation changed too.
maria: Current continuous-batcher config:
```
queue_policy: regional_soft_affinity
batch_shape:
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  max_batch_items: 64
  token_budget_target: 96
```
maria: We also flipped kernel fallback to `fast-attn-v2` for >1024 seq which may interact with batching timing.
ajay: Two hypotheses: 1) soft_affinity causes more spill under burst -> remote shots with cold KV; 2) larger token_budget_target delays batch flush and increases chance of cross-zone scheduling. Both affect tail.
kevin: Quick experiment idea: reduce token_budget_target to 64 in eu-west canary, and pin `regional_hard_affinity` for small percent of traffic to measure KV hit delta.
lina: Add a perf counter to trace: `kv_cache_warm_ms` and `remote_kv_reads`. Also include kernel selection tag in traces.
maria: Deploying a canary with token_budget_target=64 + `affinity: hard-prefer` for 5% traffic now. will post results in ~30m. @deploy-bot please note.
deploy-bot: Canary created: eu-west/affinity-canary/5% — rollout started :rocket:
sre-oncall: Heads-up — if this spikes load on primary GPU pools we should auto-scale. monitoring alert on p95>250ms already enabled.
maria: Canary finished (30m). Results: p99 down ~18% for canary slice, KV hit-rate up ~9%, remote_kv_reads down ~70%. CPU slightly up due to more local cache merges.
ajay: Nice. Any kernel-level tradeoffs? did `fast-attn-v2` show perf regressions when pinned locally?
maria: No regressions for canary; kernel timing improved slightly since no remote wait. But batch size distribution shifted — more small batches, so per-token kernel overhead rose ~3%.
kevin: Sounds like cost vs latency tradeoff. We should: 1) keep affinity hard for bursty prefixes, 2) tune token_budget_target per prefix class (short convo vs long completion), 3) explore KV-shard prefetch on spill.
lina: I'll draft a queue-policy matrix: per-region defaults, per-prefix overrides, and a canary rollout plan. Also propose an MLE to prototype background KV prefetch for hot prefixes.
maria: Agree. Filing a follow-up perf ticket with traces, canary data, and suggested defaults.
maria: TL;DR: soft-affinity + higher token_budget_target increased cross-zone cold-KV tail. Canary with lower token_budget_target + stronger affinity reduced tail at modest CPU cost. More work: per-prefix targets + prefetch.
kevin: Thanks team. Let's avoid rolling the kernel-selector change cluster-wide until we've got per-prefix budgets in place.
infra-bot: Note added to changelog: hold kernel-selector global rollout until affinity/batch heuristics validated.
sre-oncall: Marking incident as mitigated — monitoring will auto-escalate if p99 > 500ms in 5m window. :white_check_mark:
